feasibility_reasoning:
The mechanism works, but a frozen gate fails as specified.

What holds:
- Tailwind 4.3.3 inlines an @import written after other rules in place, so source order is kept. I tested this with @tailwindcss/node compile.
- The production HTML puts styles-*.css (precedence "default", byte 7316) before nes-slider-shared-v1 (7401) and nes-search-widget (18423), so their relative order is kept.
- styles.css is linked on every route, admin included (src/lib/seo/rootHead.ts:58). Admin and editor previews keep the moved rules.
- The SSR and client generators are shared (src/components/theme/css/designTokensCss.ts:25-29), so hydration parity is safe.
- No moved block contains :has().

What breaks:
- The frozen check:bundle budgets fail. publicCss: 83 (scripts/check-bundle-size.ts:2022, checked at :2580; per :1150-1158, CI ignores env overrides) goes from 80.3 to about 86.0 KiB. css: 96 (:1980) goes from 95.2 to about 100.8 KiB.
- The cascade order flips for the ticker block and the globalColors bridge. Both sit in body today, after admin-styles.css and all head sheets. Example: the bridge rule `[data-sidebar="sidebar"] a:hover:not(..):not(..){background:..!important}` (globalColors.ts:917, specificity 0,4,1) against admin-styles.css:657 (also 0,4,1, also !important). admin-styles.css then wins, so the admin sidebar style-2 hover changes.
- The .sbw sheet is per-config, not static (socialHover.ts:482, hash of the body).
- Tests break: globalColors.test.ts:186-191, sliderVariantCatalogs.test.tsx:555, sliderTypographyFidelity.test.tsx:43, plus the slider tests that check @media rules as text in <style>.
blocking_issues: check:bundle publicCss is a frozen 83 KiB budget (scripts/check-bundle-size.ts:2022/2580). The non-admin CSS goes from 80.3 to about 86.0 KiB (gzip-6, measured on the artifact with the lightningcss-minified blocks appended). The css total of 96 KiB (:1980) goes from 95.2 to about 100.8 KiB. HW-1 needs the css workstream's core split (C1/C11) first, or a reviewed budget raise.

Cascade flip for admin editors. The bridge [data-sidebar] !important rules (globalColors.ts:913-925) move from body to before admin-styles.css (linked by routes/admin.tsx:68). At equal specificity (0,4,1) the style-2 hover rule (admin-styles.css:657) then wins. Move the 13 sidebar rules into admin-styles.css or keep them in the generated block.

The .sbw social-hover sheet is config-hashed (socialHover.ts:482), not static. Hoisting it through WidgetStyleSheet into <head> changes its order relative to the body typography blocks, and the saving is only about 0.4 KB gz. Drop it from HW-1.

Tests must be rewritten: globalColors.test.ts:186-191 expects ':where(' and '@layer utilities' in globalColorsToCss({}); sliderVariantCatalogs.test.tsx:555 and sliderTypographyFidelity.test.tsx:43 assert one style[data-href=nes-slider-shared-v1]; the slider @media checks are done on <style> text. That makes effort and risk higher than 'S / low'.
effect_reasoning:
JS removed (gzip-9 on the real chunks): entry index-DPN2YAij.js -3808 B and sliderVariants-Cl4hnw1I.js -2922 B, so -6.73 KB gz. Both are High and finished before the observed FCP in prod-mobile (3182 ms and 3102 ms against FCP 3252 ms), so they are on the critical path.

CSS added: the same CSS, minified by lightningcss and appended to styles.css, adds +5.69 KB gz (+4.5 br) to the VeryHigh render-blocking sheet.

Lantern drains both through the same h2 connection at the same slope:
- Net change: -1.0 KB.
- Mobile: x 5.1-6 ms/KB = about -5 ms FCP / -6 ms LCP.
- Desktop: x 0.8 ms/KB = about 0.

HTML: -50.7 KB raw / -10.5 KB gz on psi/home.html. The workstream's own HWF-5 A/B (document -32 KB gz) shows FCP/LCP do not move, because the document finishes in parallel with the 79 KB CSS. So this gives 0 ms.

After boot-js lands (CSS becomes the long pole, the no-JS regime), the extra CSS is a cost: +5.7 KB x 5 ms/KB is about +28 ms FCP/LCP.

TBT: the rule count in the document is unchanged. CSS parsing moves into the stylesheet parse, which happens before FCP and outside the TBT window. TBT is threshold-convex. The cited -100..150 ms came from P0->P3, which also includes HW-2 and HW-3. In P1->P2, TBT is indistinguishable (median 86 -> 0-133, N=2), so none of it can be attributed to HW-1.

What-if: not run. The HTML-only transform cannot model the CSS or JS byte moves, and A/A noise (TBT up to ±464 ms) is far larger than about ±10 ms.
corrected_estimate: Mobile: FCP/LCP about -5 ms today (net -1.0 KB gz pre-FCP: JS -6.73, CSS +5.69); about +25..30 ms worse once boot-js removes JS from the FCP set; TBT 0..-15 ms. Score change about 0 points (±0.5). Desktop: 0. What remains is document weight (-50.7 KB raw / -10.5 KB gz HTML, gate inlineStyleBytes), cacheable CSS for repeat views and SPA navigation, and a smaller entry chunk. Book HW-1 as hygiene, not as score points.
